Answer: B
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates marked right lung volume reduction (hypoplasia) with an ipsilateral (rightward) mediastinal shift and a small or absent right hilar shadow, which are classic signs of unilateral pulmonary artery agenesis; the reticular pattern reflects collateral systemic circulation. Option B is the only choice that correctly identifies the ipsilateral shift associated with right-sided volume loss, whereas options suggesting contralateral shift or left-sided pathology are inconsistent with the image.
